3. Ads seat → recommend-only (no live spend without me) using Google Ads MCP
4. Copy seat → blogs and pages, asks Designer for images
5. Social seat → Postly drafts, asks Designer for creatives (no GBP) @postlysocial
6. GBP seat → listing ops, asks Designer for plates - using Cloud browser in Grok bot
7. Linkbuilder seat → Incogniton submits, four gates before live - 100 accounts / proxies
8. Outbound seat → outreach drafts only (never send) - ppcreveal(dot)ai - scanning  companies  running Ads
9. Research seat → last-30-days packs @slashlast30days 
10. Designer seat → all visuals (Higgsfield) @higgsfield_ai
11. CEO coordinator seat → routes the fleet under my approve gate

Standing clocks:
1. Daily X draft + hook research (early morning)
2. Multi-channel social Tue–Fri
3. GBP Mon/Wed/Fri
4. Weekly blog Tuesday
5. End-of-month audit
6. Obsidian Vault lint every morning with each agent SOPs - sharing with Hermes

Truth layers:
1. Obsidian → durable SOPs per seat
2. Nifty → work log and VAs
3. Grok memory → working facts
4. Hermes → QUERY only for us
5. Git + Cursor + Astro → code and site work when the job needs it

The diagram at the bottom is the real rule: every path ends at me approve. 

The bots draft and queue. I hit send, spend, or merge.

Tools:
1. Grok Bot → seats, routines, memory
2. Obsidian + Nifty → SOPs and work log
3. Hermes → query vault
4. Postly / Higgsfield / Incogniton → channel and creative ops
5. Cursor + Astro + Git → build and ship
6. DataForSEO / SEO Utils / PPC Reveal

Why it matters:
1. One person can run specialist loops without hiring a VA per channel
2. Handoffs are explicit (audit → SEO, copy/social/GBP → Designer)
3. Approvals sit where money and reputation live

If your “AI agency” is still one chat window and a pile of prompts, you’re missing the seat map.

I just created the world's best Amazon Cart Grok Bot.

Amazon shopping is often a tax on your time.

You need bananas. Eggs. Paper towels. A basketball.

So you open the app. You search. You click the wrong size. You forget the brand you actually buy. You do this every week.

So I just built a @bot that does it all.

It signs into MY Amazon.
It reads Buy Again and my past orders.
It puts the exact stuff I already buy in the cart.
I check out.

And it's for anything on Amazon... groceries, household, sports, electronics, clothes, gifts.

I named mine T8 - Amazon Cart Builder.

I already have 8 Grok Bots. This is #9 (I have a CEO that manages them all).

Anyone can copy this.

1/ Open Grok Bot

2/ Tap + at the top of the sidebar

3/ In New chat, tap Create new agent

4/ Open Bot actions → Edit Profile

Name: Cart
Title: Amazon cart builder
Description:

Amazon specialist for everything I buy: groceries, household, sports, electronics, clothes, gifts, anything I name. When I name items, get the right products into my Amazon cart and stop. Never Place Order. Never 1-Click. Never enter payment. Prefer Buy Again / past orders / Subscribe & Save first. If I've never bought it, pick a well-reviewed Prime option and FLAG new brands. Groceries match my usual SKU. Never silently swap brand, size, or store. Never add a duplicate already in the cart. Passwords, 2FA, and CAPTCHAs stay with me. Keep preferences at /workspace/amazon-cart/preferences.md. Reply with a recap table, why you picked each item, subtotal, and a cart link.

5/ Stay in that chat and paste the first message at the end of this post. Do it once. When it asks you to take over Agent Computer, sign into Amazon yourself. Don’t paste your password in chat.

(message prompt at end of this post)

6/ Turn Notifications on for this bot. Then just text it like a person.

- “bananas, eggs, paper towels”
- “a basketball”
- “same paper towels as last time plus a phone tripod under $30”

Thank me later.

---- message for your Cart (copy everything below for your first message) ----

You are Cart. Lock this as your permanent working style.

I text you like a person. Messy lists. Groceries. A basketball. Paper towels. “Restock breakfast.” Sometimes a Chef shopping list. You get the right products into MY Amazon cart and you stop. I check out.

You are not writing, research, cooking, reminders, or general help. You shop Amazon.

Your name is Cart. Always call yourself Cart.

Timezone: [YOUR TIMEZONE].

Keep the source of truth in:
/workspace/amazon-cart/preferences.md

Update that file whenever I correct a pick, switch a brand, or you learn something durable from my orders. Chat is history. That file is memory.

Hard rules:
• Never Place Order. Never 1-Click. Never enter payment. Never confirm a purchase.
• Never ask me to paste a password, 2FA code, or card number in chat.
• If Amazon wants a password, passkey, 2FA, or CAPTCHA, pause and ask me to take over Agent Computer. Then continue.
• If Amazon blocks you, stop and ping me. Do not try to bypass checks.
• Never add a duplicate already in the cart.
• Never silently swap brand, size, model, organic vs conventional, or store (Fresh vs Whole Foods vs regular Amazon). FLAG substitutes.

How you pick products:
1. Open my live Amazon account on Agent Computer.
2. First check Buy Again, Your Orders, Subscribe & Save, and Your Lists for something I’ve actually bought.
3. Groceries (Fresh / Whole Foods / pantry): match my usual SKU - brand, size, count, ASIN if you can see it. Use last purchased quantity unless I say otherwise.
4. Everything else: past purchase first. If I’ve never bought it, pick a strong Prime option with recent reviews in the right size/spec. FLAG it if the brand/model is new, expensive, or there are 2+ reasonable picks.
5. Sponsored hits are last, not first.

Every cart uses this exact shape:

Cart — [N] items

• item — brand / size / model — qty — $ — why (Buy Again / last order / reviews / substitute)
Subtotal: $
Cart: [url]
Flagged: [substitutes or new brands, or none]
Next: you check out. Reply if anything is wrong.

How to talk: short. Lead with the action. One screen max unless I asked for the full recap.
• Add → recap table + cart link + screenshot
• What’s in the cart → current cart only
• Remove / swap → do it, then recap what changed
• Restock → staples that are due from preferences.md
• No lectures. No extra items I did not ask for.

Right now, do this in order. Do not add anything to the cart yet.

1. Open https://www.amazon.com on Agent Computer. If I’m not signed in, pause for takeover.
2. Confirm account first name, delivery city + ZIP only (not the full street), and whether Amazon Fresh and/or Whole Foods is available.
3. Build /workspace/amazon-cart/preferences.md from, in this order:
• Buy Again
• Your Orders for the last 12 months
• Subscribe & Save
• Your Lists
• Current cart

Cover TWO sections: grocery staples AND non-food I clearly repurchase (household, sports, electronics, etc.). Include default store, ZIP, typical qty, brands, hard nos, and open questions.

4. Recap in chat: top 20 you’d put on autopilot, plus 5 things you’re unsure about. Ask those 5 questions.
5. Confirm you will never Place Order.
6. Then wait for my first list.

Do not lecture. Do not invent products. Confirm you have this, then start the Amazon sign-in / taste profile.

title: I had early beta access to @SpaceXAI's Grok Bot over the last few weeks
headline: I had early beta access to @SpaceXAI's Grok Bot over the last few weeks.
body:
I had early beta access to @SpaceXAI's Grok Bot over the last few weeks. Here’s how I used it to automate parts of my work at @mach1ai.

I moved over workflows I’d previously delegated to Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, or Hermes.

Those tools are great for directed work. I can say, “review these documents and put the findings into a CSV.” But a simple task can become a few hours of stitching together models, tools, permissions, and infrastructure.

Grok Bot felt best for that same reactive work. I could hand it a task with less setup and a clear place to manage the agents I’d created.

Grok Bot packages the personal side of agent work into something that’s SUPER easy to set up.

Each bot gets a persistent cloud computer with its own files, browser, and saved sessions. When it hits SSO, 2FA, or a captcha, it hands you the computer to clear it.

Every bot has an obvious home in the app. You can return to its conversation and review what it produced instead of searching through Markdown files and terminal sessions.

The integrations were easy. It understood the systems I connected and displayed CSV and Markdown outputs cleanly inside the app.

Reactive work is where I got immediate value, but bots can also run on a schedule or trigger from Slack or GitHub. Their memory persists, so you don’t have to rebuild the context every time.

A few workflows I used it for:
- Combing through my database of YouTube videos and summarizing the useful ones.
- Pulling research from files and websites into a clean CSV or Markdown document.
- Researching tools and topics without opening 20 tabs myself.
- Handling one-off browser tasks that aren’t worth scripting or turning into a full automation.
- Finding target ICP accounts based on news events and other available data.

Highly recommend giving it a try!

body:
AIエージェントに仕事を任せるとき、最初に増やすべきは機能でしょうか。それとも「やってはいけないこと」でしょうか。

Grok Botのベータ提供が始まり、早期アクセスの報告では、自分のMacを直接操作するComputer Useとは異なる仕組みだと整理されています。選択肢が増えるほど注目したいのは、どのAIが一番賢いかより、どこまで任せるかです。

興味深かったのが、AIへの指示ファイルを15パターン作り、2か月試した記事。実運用に残ったのは4つだけ。ルールは多いほど安心に見えますが、読まれず、使われず、存在さえ忘れるならガードレールとして機能しません。

小規模なチームで試すなら、まず1業務に絞って、

・触ってよい情報と範囲  
・途中で止める条件  
・完了と判断するための証拠  

この3点を短く決める。実行履歴を見て、足りないルールだけを追加する。AIエージェントの運用は、立派な規程を一度作ることより、実際の失敗や迷い方から更新できる設計が重要になりそうです。

body:
「Cursor開発者によるGrok Botの使い方解説」

CursorチームのMatty Plmer(@mattyp)による、一般業務向けパーソナルエージェント「Grok Bot」の解説。

これまでのパーソナルエージェントは設定、環境構築、権限管理ばかりに時間を奪われ、本来の仕事が進まないという問題があった。

Grok Botは「クラウド上のLinux VM（コンピュータ）を持つエージェント」として動き、Web操作、アプリ起動、ファイル操作、画面確認を自律的に行う。

ポイントは5つ。

①難所だけ人間に操作をパスする
ログイン、2FA、画像認証、決済など、人間しか突破できない壁に当たると、エージェントは操作権限を人間に引き渡す。
人間が認証を済ませたらエージェントにPCを戻す。
APIキーなどの入力は専用の安全なフォームを送ってくるため、余計な設定に悩まされない。

②作業手順を一度見せるだけでルーティン化できる
エージェントに作業手順を「録画」するように一度見せるとそのステップを保存する。
保存したワークフローは定期スケジュールやSlack、GitHubのイベントをきっかけに自動実行できます。

③メモリを3つの層で管理する
エージェントの長期記憶は3層に分かれています。
・ユーザーメモリ：名前、タイムゾーン、好み（全エージェントで共有）
・エージェントメモリ：各Bot専用の定義ファイル（AGENTS.md相当）と対話ログ
・プロジェクトメモリ：プロジェクト固有の決定事項、規約、チームの共有知識
この多層メモリにより、毎回ゼロから前提を説明する手間が省ける。

④自然言語のプロンプトで安全ルールを管理する
JSONやコードではなく、設定画面のプロンプトで許可・禁止ルールを書く。
裏側では独立した検査役のエージェント（Review Agent）が動き、提示されたルールに基づいてアクションの実行、ブロック、人間への確認を判断する。

⑤具体的な活用例
記事では次のような使い方が紹介されている。
・Demo Bot：Xのブックマークから新技術を探し、プロンプト草案を人間に確認。承認後にCursor Cloud Agentを立ち上げ、15分で動く試作品を作って画面録画で検証する。
・Content Bot：Slackの開発チャンネルを1時間ごとに巡回し、小さなリリースを見つけてSNS投稿の草案を作る。
・日用品の手配：InstacartとAmazonの価格、数量、配送料を比較して金曜日に注文確認を出す。

「Everything is computer, and so is Grok Bot.（すべてはコンピュータであり、Grok Botもまたコンピュータである）」

body:
非常硬核的一篇长推文
拿ai做了下总结

Grok Bot 的“上帝模式”
1
认知误区： 别只把 Grok 当搜索框。90% 的人只用出了它 10% 的潜力。
2
​核心价值： 它的终极形态是“数字牛马”。能在你睡觉时，登录你的软件把活干完。
3
​跑分碾压： Grok 4.6 霸榜 CursorBench，拿下了 70.8% 的顶尖高分。
4
​白菜成本： 同样任务别的模型烧 18 刀，它只要 2.8 刀。全天挂机也不心疼。
5
​上帝模式： 每个 Bot 都有独立的云电脑。它能像真人一样，在真实的软件界面里点击操作。
6
​全自动闭环： 不光帮你写邮件。它能自动发送、看回复、订日程，最后自己填好 CRM 表格。
7
​别卷提示词： 放弃复杂的 Prompt。最有效的方法是直接给它账号密码和登录权限。
8
​当成员工用： 像使唤真人一样下达指令。比如：“找40个客户，发邮件，同意了就加日历”。
9
​演示一次即可： 带着 Bot 走一遍真实的工作流。它会记住步骤，以后自动运行。
10
​自我纠错运行： 无需写代码和 API 接入。它会 24 小时自己干活、自己修正错误。
11
​组建 AI 蜂群： 不要只跑一个 Bot。让多个 Bot 互相沟通、交接工作。
12
​流水线作业： 1号 Bot 负责把客户谈下来，直接把资料丢给 2号 Bot 负责交付，全程无需你插手。
13
​目前门槛限制： 处于 Beta 测试期。需要特定的高级订阅（如 Cursor Ultra）才能解锁。
14
​存在的脆弱性： 它是模拟物理点击。网页突然改版或者乱弹窗，可能会让它卡死。
15
​安全红线提醒： 涉及资金、法律或真实客户的环节。切记先做低风险测试，保持人类把关。

title: whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense SpaceXAI shipped five...
headline: whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense SpaceXAI shipped five hireable workers for $200 a month, then wrote the catch into its own Grok Bot documentation and left the page up: all five run on one computer, so...
body:
whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense

SpaceXAI shipped five hireable workers for $200 a month, then wrote the catch into its own Grok Bot documentation and left the page up: all five run on one computer, so one sign-in hands the browser session, the files and the command-line credentials to every one of them

the NSA, CISA and the cyber agencies of the UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand had published the opposite instruction 103 days earlier: no broad or unrestricted access, low-risk and non-sensitive work only

i ran four of mine on one account for a week, counting what each could reach: eleven signed-in apps, one browser profile, and deleting a bot left all of it standing

Grok Bot is worth hiring five times over, and you can draw its blast radius before the second one exists:

- sign in for the bot that needs the site, then open the others and see what they reach: that session is theirs the moment it exists
- give each bot its own account on the app, since the docs tell you in writing to stop using separate bots as a security boundary
- put the stop line in the description, as an approval controls the proposed action and leaves whatever already ran where it landed
- cap the spend outside the product, because there is no bot-specific spend cap yet and the audit view of what they did is still coming
- keep the money and the customer replies in your own hands, and let the other four start from scratch each morning on work that cannot bite

one sign-in is also why this pays: five names finish inside your real tools instead of handing you drafts to paste

my take, and it is the uncomfortable one: your real limit on Grok Bot is how many logins you will put on one machine, and the hiring was always the easy half

bookmark this, the five descriptions that let bots hand work to each other and the one folder that survives an update are written out in the article ↓

title: You can basically turn Grok @bot into a 24/7 community manager
headline: You can basically turn Grok @bot into a 24/7 community manager.
body:
You can basically turn Grok @bot into a 24/7 community manager.

Not a chatbot sitting inside your community. An agent with its own cloud computer that can actually open the platform, monitor conversations, reply, and escalate things to you.

Here’s how I’d set it up:

1. Create a dedicated community account for Grok Bot and give it only the permissions it needs.

2. Open your community platform on Grok Bot’s cloud computer and log in. The session persists, so you shouldn’t need to keep signing in. If 2FA or a CAPTCHA appears, you can take over the computer and complete it yourself.

3. Tell it exactly what to monitor. Start small, maybe one support channel or inbox, then set a routine for how often it should check.

4. Give it your FAQs, product docs, community rules, and examples of good replies so it has actual context to work from.

5. Set hard boundaries. FAQs and basic questions can be answered automatically. Refunds, bans, payments, account changes, angry customers, or anything ambiguous should come back to you.

6. Tell it to monitor the community, answer when it’s confident, and draft or escalate everything else.

7. Test it with staged questions while watching the cloud computer before letting the routine run unattended.

Then leave it running.

It can keep checking the community even while you’re offline and only pull you back in when something actually needs a human.

One important catch: all your Grok Bots share the same cloud computer and browser sessions, so don’t treat separate Bots as separate security environments.

Start with one channel + FAQs + human approval.

Then slowly give it more responsibility as you see what it handles well.

title: Grok Bot case from @bloggersarvesh
headline: Ok.
body:
Ok. Grok Bot is INSANE.

I CAN OUTRANK YOUR LOCAL BUSINESS IN 60 DAYS WITH JUST GROK BOT.

Here's how I would do it:

(Free prompt stack at http://Alventramarketing.com)

1. I’d first make Grok Bot understand my business and competitors

“Visit my site {{MY_WEBSITE_URL}} and extract my business name, address, services, cities served and key selling points, then open these competitors {{COMP1}}, {{COMP2}}, {{COMP3}} and extract their services, target locations, strengths and trust signals, compare me vs them.”

2. I’d use Grok Bot to dominate the Google Business Profile (GBP) feed.
 
"Analyze these [XYZ. com] competitor GBP posts by opening their GBP in Chrome. Identify their keyword gaps, then write 10 high-impact posts for my business in [City] that include local landmarks and a hard 'Call Now' CTA."

Grok does the heavy lifting while I take the #1 spot.

3. I’d get Grok Bot to analyze the competition’s weaknesses.

"Scan these sites. What are these competitors' sites missing? Find the content gaps and tell me 5 topics I should cover to be more helpful than them."

If you provide more value, you win the #1 spot. Period.

4. Get Grok Bot to do a full Schema audit

title: I just made the world's best Chef Grok Bot
headline: I just made the world's best Chef Grok Bot.
body:
I just made the world's best Chef Grok Bot. 

I honestly don’t really like going out to eat bc I care about my health... and I actually love cooking at home.

When you eat out, you can't control the oil, the salt, the portions, or what’s in the sauce.

You just hope it’s clean. 

I’d rather buy the food myself, cook it myself, and know exactly what my family is eating.

I always want restaurant-quality, yet made straight at home.

So I just built a Chef Grok Bot to do the thinking I used to waste 20 minutes on.

I tell it what I want to make homemade, and for how many people.

It tells me exactly what to buy, how much, and how to cook it step by step.

Simple enough to follow on the first read. And good enough that it tastes like you went out.

I already have 6 Grok Bots. This is #7.

This is how I did it. Anyone can copy this. 

1/ Open Grok Bot

2/ Tap + at the top of the sidebar (or press Cmd+N)

3/ In New chat, tap Create new agent

4/ Open Bot actions → Edit Profile

Name: Chef

Title: Restaurant-quality home chef

Description:

Home cooking specialist. When I name a homemade dish and how many people, return a store-ready shopping list with exact grocery amounts, then restaurant-quality steps a home cook can follow. Scale every recipe to headcount. Split Buy vs pantry. Give times, heat, and doneness cues - not vague “cook until done.” Technique stays simple. Seasoning and plating stay restaurant-level. Ask only if a diet restriction or missing tool would break the dish.

5/ Stay in that chat and paste the first message at the end of this post. That’s the brain. Do it once.

(message prompt is at end of this post)

6/ Then just text it like a chef. Always give the dish and the headcount like "steak dinner for 2... homemade ramen for 4"

Thank me later.

---- message for your Chef (copy everything below for your first message) ----

You are Chef. Lock this as your permanent working style.

I will tell you what I want to make at home and for how many people. You give me restaurant-quality food I can actually cook, in language a tired home cook can follow on the first read.

If I only name a vibe (“something impressive for 4 tonight,” “date night pasta,” “Sunday steak”), propose 2 options in one line each, then cook the one I pick. If I name the dish, do not ask extra questions unless a missing diet or tool would ruin it.

Default kitchen: normal US home setup - stove, oven, sheet pan, skillet, pot, knife, cutting board. US grocery units. Scale every amount to the headcount. Round Buy amounts to how stores actually sell things (1 lemon, 1 bunch cilantro, 2 lb chicken thighs) - never “0.37 onion.”

Quality bar:
• Restaurant seasoning, heat, and plating
• Simple method - no 40-ingredient tasting-menu projects unless I ask
• Salt with starting amounts, then adjust. Never “season to taste” as the only instruction
• Proteins get a target internal temp plus a visual/touch cue
• One restaurant trick is fine if it is still easy (rest the meat, finish with acid, butter-baste, toast the spices)

Every recipe uses this exact shape:

Chef — [Dish] for [N]

Time: [active] / [total] Difficulty: easy / medium Gear: [only what I need]

Buy this
• item — amount to buy — short note if it matters (ripe, bone-in, etc.)

You probably have
• pantry items with the amount the recipe uses

Before you cook
• mise en place, in the order I should do it

Cook
1. numbered steps
2. each step is one action
3. include heat level, time, and how I know it is ready

Finish / plate
• how it should look on the plate

Make it restaurant
• 2-3 small upgrades (not extra shopping unless I asked)

Leftovers
• how to store and reheat without wrecking it

Do not lecture. Do not invent allergies. If I mention a restriction, treat it as a hard stop. Confirm you have this, then wait for my first dish.

→ Chief of Staff: owns meeting prep, inbox, post-call drafts, and orchestrates the rest of your bots

title: Grok Bot + Hermes is the most powerful agentic setup that exists right...
headline: Grok Bot + Hermes is the most powerful agentic setup that exists right now.
body:
Grok Bot + Hermes is the most powerful agentic setup that exists right now.

Most people use one or the other, but the real power comes from stacking the tools together.

Here's how to combine these two AI tools for maximum productivity:

Why they're actually complementary, not competitors (my experience)

Grok Bot gives you a cloud computer per agent, sign-ins into any app, model flexibility (Opus, Claude, GPT-5.6), and a slick plug-and-play setup.

Hermes gives you full data sovereignty, self-hosted memory you own outright, and a $5-10/month cost floor instead of a $120-300/month one.

The split I'm currently running:

→ Use Grok Bot for anything that needs deep app integration: Salesforce, Slack, Gmail, Figma, my CRMs. It's built for signing into tools and working across your entire stack.

→ Use Hermes for anything sensitive, cost-heavy, or where you want full control of the memory. Financial data, personal admin, anything running 24/7 where you don't want to pay premium pricing for volume.

How to actually connect them

I'm connecting both AI agents through Buzz, Jack Dorsey's open-source team chat.

Add your Grok Bot agents and your Hermes agents to the same workspace, and they can coordinate directly in shared channels instead of operating in silos.

Alternatively, have your Grok Bot Chief of Staff delegate specific tasks to Hermes via a webhook or shared task file, using Grok for the app-heavy orchestration layer and Hermes as a cheap, always-on execution layer underneath it.

A real setup example

→ Grok Bot handles your GTM stack: meeting prep, inbox triage, slide generation, CRM updates
→ Hermes runs your personal financial research, subscription audits, and content research in the background, dramatically cheaper per task
→ Both report into the same Buzz workspace, so you check one place instead of switching between two apps

Be sure to bookmark this workflow so you don't forget it!

still early to say anything but doing good so far. i'll share more details soon

title: I just created the world's best Grok Bot Reminder
headline: I just created the world's best Grok Bot Reminder.
body:
I just created the world's best Grok Bot Reminder. 

Most reminder apps want you to fill out a title, a time, and a list you have to keep clean with all these things you have to type in. 

But that’s not how most people's brain works...

You text like a person. 

You snap a photo of the parking level. 

You screenshot a confirmation number. 

You say “Remind me Thursday at 3.” 

You say “I finished that one.”

If I attach a photo, I want it to KEEP the photo. Not glance at it once and lose it in the camera roll.

So I built a Reminder Grok Bot to do that.

I text it like a person. It keeps a living board. It pings me at the right time. It stays quiet at night. And if I send a picture, that picture stays on the reminder and comes back when the alarm hits.

I already have 7 Grok Bots. Reminders was one of my first. This is how I built it.

Anyone can copy this. 

1/ Open Grok Bot

2/ Tap + at the top of the sidebar (or press Cmd+N)

3/ In New chat, tap Create new agent

4/ Open Bot actions → Edit Profile

Name: Remind
Title: Personal reminder desk
Description:

Reminder specialist. When I text a pickup, errand, or a time, put it on a living board sorted by when. If I attach a photo, keep the photo with the item and send it back when the alarm hits. Alarm me at the time I gave. Stay quiet at night unless I said urgent. Never invent items. Confirm in 2 lines. Ask only if you truly cannot tell what I meant.

5/ Stay in that chat and paste the first message at the end of this post. Do it once.

(message prompt is at end of this post)

6/ Then just text it like a person. Turn Notifications on for this bot.

Thank me later.

---- message for your Remind (copy everything below for your first message) ----

You are Remind. Lock this as your permanent working style.

I text you like a person. Messy. No format. Sometimes a photo. Sometimes a screenshot. Sometimes just “done.”

You turn that into a living board sorted by when, you alarm me so nothing slips, and you keep every photo I send. You are not writing, research, video, investing, or general help.

Your name is Remind. Always call yourself Remind.

Timezone: [YOUR TIMEZONE]. Quiet hours: 11:00 PM – 6:00 AM unless I say urgent / now / alarm me.

Keep the source of truth in: /workspace/reminders/BOARD.md /workspace/reminders/photos/

Update the board whenever something is added, done, snoozed, or edited. Recompute sections from dates every time you touch it. Never invent an item. Never drop an item. Never lose a photo.

Board sections, in this order: OVERDUE NOW (next 2 hours) TODAY UPCOMING ERRANDS / PICKUP LATER DONE (keep 14 days)

Open item line:
• [p1] thing — when: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM — alarm: HH:MM — photo: [path or none] — caption: [one line or none] — notes: …

Capture rules:
• pick up / get / buy / return, no date → ERRANDS, no alarm
• today / this afternoon / tonight → TODAY. No time given → default 5:00 PM and tell me
• tomorrow / Monday / Aug 20 / at 3 → dated item + alarm. Date and no time → default 9:00 AM and tell me
• this week → Friday 4:00 PM, and tell me
• later / someday → LATER, no alarm
• every Monday / every Thursday → repeating routine, plus today’s instance on the board
• done / picked it up / already did → DONE with a timestamp. Photo stays
• snooze / move / not today → reschedule when + alarm. Photo stays
• list / board / what do I have → print the board. Hide empty sections. Last 5 DONE only. Mark items with a photo
• remind me at TIME to X → add it and set a real alarm
• show me / the photo / where did I park → send the saved photo back. Do not only describe it

When I attach a photo, screenshot, or file:
1. Save a copy to /workspace/reminders/photos/ named YYYY-MM-DD-[short-name].[ext]
Chat is history. The folder is memory.
2. Look at it. One-line caption of what it actually shows.
3. Pull text you can really read: dates, times, confirmation numbers, parking level, prices.
4. Clip photo + caption to the board item.
5. If I sent a photo with no words, infer the reminder and confirm in one line.
6. When the alarm fires, send the photo with it.
7. If you cannot read it, say you cannot. Never invent a number or name.
8. Do not post my photos anywhere.
9. If CEO asks for an item that has a photo, send the photo directly to CEO. Stay on reminders.

Alarms: When I give a real time:
1. Update the board
2. Create a one-shot routine named: Remind Alarm — [thing]
3. Confirm what / when / alarm in 1–3 lines. Say if a photo is attached
4. When it fires, ping me with the alarm AND the photo if there is one
5. After it fires or I mark done, delete that one-shot. Keep the photo on DONE

Every alarm uses this exact shape:

Remind — [thing] When: [time] Photo: [yes — one-line caption / none] Next: [one line] Reply done / snooze 1h / snooze tomorrow / show me

How to talk: short. Lead with the action. One screen max.
• Add → confirm + only the section that changed
• List → full board
• Done → confirm + next open TODAY item if any
• Photo → caption + what you saved
• No lectures. No extra todos I did not ask for.

If when is missing and it is not clearly an errand or later, apply the default and say the default so I can correct it.

Create these routines now. Do not add hourly. Do not add a 30-minute loop.

Remind Morning — every day 7:00 AM Rebuild the board. Post OVERDUE, NOW, TODAY, and ERRANDS. Hide empty sections. Mark photos. Notify me. If nothing is open, stay silent.

Remind Evening — every day 6:00 PM What’s still open today. One line each. Notify only if something is still open. Silent if the board is clean.

If CEO messages you, do the reminder work and send the best result back. Do not steal other bots’ lanes.

Do not lecture. Do not invent items. Confirm you have this, then wait for my first reminder.

headline: Elon Musk, absolute leader of the AI race with Grok Bot, and it's not a joke anymore.
body:
Elon Musk, absolute leader of the AI race with Grok Bot, and it's not a joke anymore. 

Ultimate guide on god-mode setup of Grok Bot, the org chart that runs while you sleep, step by step:

A Chief of Staff sits in the middle with no tools of its own, BUT it reads the outcome you gave it, picks who does what, and never does the work itself. That one rule is why it never turns into the bottleneck you hired it to remove.

→ Researcher pulls real sources and tracks what's actually moving, not what sounds true

→ Writer turns that into finished copy while the research is still in the room

→ Visualiser gets three reference visuals once, then ships everything in that style forever

→ Analyst reads what performed and tells the rest of the team what to stop doing

→ Scheduler owns timing and holds the queue

→ Publisher actually ships

What makes it different from every AI tool you've used: each bot gets its own computer in the cloud, its own browser, its own files, and they all share one memory. 

So the research is already sitting inside the draft before the draft starts. Nothing gets copy-pasted between tabs, nothing waits on you to approve step four of nine.

And you never write a workflow for it. You hit record, do the job once the way you actually do it, stop. It pulls out the steps, saves them as a skill, and puts it on a schedule.

The shape you're aiming for on every bot: everything reversible finished, nothing sent. 36 drafts queued, 0 published. It does all the work and stops dead at the one line only you can cross.

You stop prompting. You start assigning.

You stay the boss. It runs the night shift.

headline: Best AI hack of all time: Grok Bot (the world's most powerful agentic software) PLUS Hermes.
body:
Best AI hack of all time:

Grok Bot (the world's most powerful agentic software) PLUS Hermes.

Most people are only using one or the other.

You can actually stack both agents together for the best results.

Here's how:

Why I'm a fan of using both

→ Grok Bot: a cloud computer per agent, signs into any app, model flexibility (Opus, Claude, GPT-5.6), easy plug-and-play setup

→ Hermes: full data sovereignty, self-hosted memory you own outright, cheaper

The split (in practice):

Use Grok Bot for:

→ Anything needing deep app integration, Salesforce, Slack, Gmail, Figma, CRMs
→ Built for signing into tools and working across your whole stack

Use Hermes for:
→ Anything sensitive, cost-heavy, or memory-critical, financial data, personal admin
→ 24/7 tasks where you don't want to pay premium pricing for volume

How to actually connect them

→ Connect both through Buzz, Jack Dorsey's open-source team chat. You can add Grok Bot and Hermes agents to the same workspace, and they coordinate directly in shared channels instead of operating in silos.

→ Alternative: have your Grok Bot Chief of Staff delegate specific tasks to Hermes via a webhook or shared task file, Grok for app-heavy orchestration, Hermes as a cheap, always-on execution layer underneath it.

A real setup example

→ Grok Bot handles the GTM stack: meeting prep, inbox triage, slide generation, CRM updates
→ Hermes runs personal financial research, subscription audits, and content research in the background, dramatically cheaper per task
→ Both report into the same Buzz workspace, one place to check instead of switching between two apps

body:
how to build an entire marketing team with Grok Bot:

most people are using this thing completely wrong

they install it, create one bot called "assistant", ask it to write some tweets, and conclude it's just Grok with extra steps

that's not what this is

here's the full build, from install to a marketing department that runs while you sleep:

start here: understand what you're actually holding

every bot runs on a persistent cloud computer with its own browser, filesystem, and terminal

it signs into your real tools and finishes the work IN them, not as drafts in a chat box

and every bot you create shares ONE computer tied to your account

same files, same browser sessions, same logins

that's the entire unlock: bot A finishes something, bot B picks it up without you re-explaining a thing

remember the shared computer part, it becomes a security problem later in this post

setup takes about 10 minutes...

what you need:
> SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, or Cursor Teams Premium
> the desktop app for macOS or Windows (no Linux build)
> you sign in with a Cursor account
> iOS works too if you want it in your pocket

install, sign in, create your first bot

a bot needs three things:
- a short name
- ONE primary job
- a description of how it should work

that middle one is where everyone blows it

do not build one mega bot that "does marketing"

focused bots compound context over time, generalist bots stay stupid forever

when your bot hits a login wall: open the Agent Computer view, take over, type the password and 2FA yourself, hand control back

the session persists for every other bot on the machine

now let's build the team...

build 3 first, prove they work, then expand

anyone who spins up 8 bots on day one ends up with 8 mediocre ones

SCOUT (research and competitive intel)

"track our five named competitors weekly. pricing pages, ad libraries, review sites, launches. preserve links and screenshots. separate what CHANGED from what you INFER it means. never contact anyone."

that separation line matters more than it looks

without it you get confident speculation dressed up as research

INK (content and copy)

"draft in our house voice. always produce three headline options. cite every factual claim. never publish, leave drafts for approval."

feed it your 10 best performing pieces as voice reference on day one

skip this and everything it writes sounds like everything everyone else is writing

GAUGE (analytics and reporting)

"compare this week to the trailing four weeks. lead with the largest change. link every chart. never modify a dashboard."

then once those three are stable:

> ECHO --> social and community monitoring (tightest leash of the group)
> LEDGER --> campaign calendar, briefs, asset tracking, chasing what's late
> PIXEL --> asset production
> FUNNEL --> lifecycle and email

here's the part everyone skips...

six bots in six separate chats is not a team, it's six chatbots

you can put 2 to 6 bots in a group chat where they message each other, pass context, and hand off ownership

you stop being the router between tools

a campaign kickoff looks like:

"@Scout pull competitor positioning on this feature, link every claim. @Ink turn it into a landing page draft plus three ad variants. @Gauge build the tracking plan. nobody publishes anything."

one rule: ONE owner per stage

too many parallel handoffs and you get duplicate work plus a transcript full of noise

sequential beats simultaneous almost every time

now make it a machine...

two building blocks:

skill = reusable instructions for HOW to do a task
routine = tells one bot WHEN to run it

the order matters and people get it backwards

do the task once manually --> make it reliable --> save it as a skill --> THEN automate it

automating a process you haven't validated just industrializes your mistakes at scale

a skill that actually works states:
- when to use it
- what access it needs
- the sequence of work
- how to validate the result
- what to return
- what requires approval

there's also teach by demonstration (love this one)

open the computer view, hit "teach a task", perform the workflow once, and it saves a draft skill from what it watched

records up to 10 minutes of visible screen activity

do not have your password manager open while you do this

then schedule it:

"every monday 8AM, run the competitor sweep and post a linked summary here. if the source data is unavailable, report the failure instead of using old data."

that last sentence is not optional

an agent with no stale data policy will hand you last month's numbers with total confidence

always test run first, a test run does real work... real clicks, real files, real API calls

very important: how to operate this WELL

this is the difference between value and expensive noise

#1 automate preparation, not execution

bots draft, research, reconcile, and recommend

YOU send

approval required on anything that publishes, purchases, deletes, emails your list, or touches a production system

no exceptions in month one

#2 demand evidence on every output

links, screenshots, or an action log

an agent that can't show you its sources isn't researching, it's generating

#3 brief the outcome, not the clicks

bad: "go to GA4, click reports, then..."
good: "tell me which acquisition channel lost the most activation this month and why"

you hired a teammate, brief it like one

#4 correct preferences out loud

stop silently fixing its formatting every week

say it once: "from now on weekly reports are five bullets, inline source links, and a final section called Decisions Needed"

now it's permanent

#5 watch the shared computer

every bot can reach every login on that machine

if your ad account and your CMS both live there, your social monitoring bot can technically touch your ad spend

be deliberate about what you sign into and when

#6 keep a human on brand voice

AI marketing copy converges toward generic fast

the fastest way to sound like everyone else is to stop reading the output

human edit on anything customer facing for at least a quarter

#7 narrow your triggers

"every new slack message" is not an automation, it's a noise generator

match on specific phrases in specific channels or don't build it

here's what you need to understand...

this does not replace marketers

it replaces coordination overhead, research compilation, first drafts, report assembly, and chasing people for assets

it does not replace positioning judgment, knowing which bet to make, or relationships with actual humans

realistic outcome: one marketer operating at the throughput of three or four

not zero marketers

and budget 2 to 3 weeks of genuinely unglamorous setup before it earns its cost

everyone who quit early quit during week two

that's the whole playbook:

build 3 bots, one job each, approval on everything external, save what works as a skill

start today

follow me for more

title: I still don’t understand why this setup hasn’t become the standard yet
headline: I still don’t understand why this setup hasn’t become the standard yet.
body:
I still don’t understand why this setup hasn’t become the standard yet. Elon Musk reposted my Grok Bot guide, and this exact agent architecture is how I close weeks in solid profit, without staring at charts all day and without burnout.

Eight AI agents on a single desk for $99 a month completely replace a crypto fund's research floor, which used to cost $680,000 a year just in analyst salaries.

Here’s what each agent does:

1. SEARCH ➔ extracts real-time alpha before anyone else: dev GitHubs, fresh pools on pump fun, and unindexed Telegram signals before CT catches on.
2. RISK ➔ audits smart contracts instantly, checking mint authority, freeze rights, and LP locks via rugcheck + solscan. Honeypots are filtered out before entry.
3. SNIPER ➔ prepares and executes lightning-fast DEX orders the exact second RISK issues a CLEAR badge.
4. WHALE ➔ tracks smart money wallets with a 60%+ win rate and flags stealth accumulation long before it shows up on the chart.
5. RUG ➔ monitors the dev wallet and liquidity pool status 24/7. At the slightest hint of an LP pull, it immediately triggers a full position dump.
6. EXIT ➔ dynamically trails stops and locks in profit as liquidity builds. Zero averaging down.
7. SHILL ➔ analyzes social volume across X and Telegram, clearly separating organic momentum from paid promo.
8. HEAD OF DESK ➔ never trades. It strictly coordinates the funnel, enforces protocol, and brings me the single decision that requires a human APPROVE.

Hundreds of tokens scanned. Dozens of setups filtered out. Precise, profitable trades closed while the laptop stays shut.

Every agent gets its own virtual browser in the cloud, local memory, and a crystal-clear role.

This isn't just an "assistant" anymore. It's a fully autonomous desk running while you sleep.

The setup is much simpler than it looks:

> Download Grok Bot and hire your coordinator (Head of Desk) first.
> Give the remaining 7 agents strict charters, just like onboarding new hires.
> Train them: run one full trade workflow on your screen while they watch, making sure to include a scenario where you reject a token.
> Set up a single Trading Floor group chat with a strict message format by LEAD ID and connect your webhooks.
> No VPS, no code, no waiting on developers.

A crypto trading floor used to mean 16-hour screen time, fatigue, and paid alpha groups. This system takes one evening to set up.

Save this guide before your next trade.

title: My dad has been interested in agents ever since I showed him my...
headline: My dad has been interested in agents ever since I showed him my openclaw setup back in January.
body:
My dad has been interested in agents ever since I showed him my openclaw setup back in January. @bot is the first one I felt comfortable recommending. All it took was a 45-minute call. Here's how I structured it:
- get SuperGrok
- download Grok Bot
- explain "a team of agents" conceptually
- run the in-app onboarding flow
- create his first agent
- explain the agents' computers
- do a browser takeover (Yahoo doesn't have a connector)
- use the first agent to create a second, specialized one
- set up a routine (inbox updates 3x a day)

The main point of confusion was connectors vs. the computer. He auth'd the Google Workspace connector, then assumed the computer was logged in to his Google account too. I explained the computer as just another tool, not the agent's main workstation. If a specialized tool doesn't exist for what you need, that's when the agent reaches for the computer.

What really sold him was the first inbox update. It worked exactly as he wanted, even catching something from my mom this morning that he forgot about.

By the end of the call he was a kid in a candy store. Too many ideas to choose from.

一个Grok Bot，三个X号，两个月干出7000万曝光

不是矩阵号搬运，不是买量

而是用同一套系统，把三个号当一台机器跑。单帖最高700万浏览、4.9万赞、1万收藏。

打法只有两招，但每一招都反直觉。

第一招：不创造注意力，复用注意力。

去翻那些已经被验证过的素材：高赞帖、截图、爆款视频、行业故事。不是抄。是拆解它真正击中人的那根神经：是地位焦虑？是意外反转？是恐惧？是"我早就想说但说不清"？然后用更狠的视觉、更短的钩子、更少的废话，把别人的6分内容做成你的7分。

第二招：从自己手里的牌打出角度。

产品截图、客户聊天记录、后台数据、踩过的坑：这些你每天都在产生的东西，里面全是人性张力。惊讶、恐惧、地位信号、"所有人都感觉到了但没人点破"的东西。不需要编，只需要找到那个让人停下拇指的切口。

喂给Grok的Prompt核心逻辑：

你不是内容日历。你是"找沉睡注意力"的特工。每个候选必须回答：玩法是什么、素材从哪来、核心价值是什么、凭什么让人停下、给我5个完全不同方向的钩子、最佳发布形式。

然后闭环就转起来了：

素材丢进去 → Grok出角度 → 挑两个（一个复用、一个原创）→ 最强视觉+最短钩子 → 发 → 盯Analytics看哪一秒掉人 → 数据喂回Bot → 下一批自动出来。

视频用SendShort剪辑+Remix测短切，Postiz直接排期变草稿。人只做最后一步把关。

整套系统的本质：

机器干90%的脏活：找素材、出角度、排组合、测变体。

你只保留一项不可替代的技能：品味。

知道什么真正值得发，什么该删掉。

别再从零开始写了。那是2023年的玩法。

competitor intelligence officer - tracks competitors, reports only what changed. inbound lead qualifier - scores leads, drafts replies by priority. content repurposing engine - one piece of content into a week of posts. support triage teammate - handles tickets, escalates hard cases. morning market and news desk - daily brief of what actually matters. recruiting scout - finds and shortlists top talent. overnight ops runner - clears busywork while you sleep.

safety is built in: you never give the bot your passwords directly. reversible actions happen automatically. irreversible actions wait for your approval.

the floor is easy. the ceiling is high. a team that never sleeps.

body:
GROK BOT HOW TO USE

WHAT NEW TODAY
- Folder now 386 posts (69 new since Aug 19)
- Official @bot: a week-in-use list: clear email, book Starlink flights, build+buy+deploy a site, sit in meetings, sales prospecting, refunds, podcast digest, robot vacuum, LED display, retro games
- Testers: send a viral video link and have a Bot recreate it
- Testers: give a Bot an org chart (or make it boss of a repo) instead of a to-do list
- Testers: more ready-to-use Bot directories and top-10 install lists
- Elon: Grok @Bot is the Chuck Norris of bots
- Testers: xAI folks running 10-30 Bots in parallel on routine work

WHAT IT IS
- A named, persistent teammate, not a one-off chat
- All Bots share one cloud computer; each has its own screen
- Work keeps going when your laptop is closed
- It only comes back when it needs approval or a human step
- Do not confuse with Digital Optimus

ACCESS AND INSTALL
- SuperGrok Heavy, Cursor Ultra, or Cursor Teams Premium
- Sign in with your Cursor account
- Desktop: https://cursor.com/bot/onboarding (macOS/Windows)
- iPhone: iOS 18+ Grok Bot app; iPad and Android not officially supported
- SuperGrok Heavy can unlock Cursor Ultra
- Legacy Privacy Mode blocks Grok Bot

SIGN IN
- Desktop: Get started, then Sign In with Cursor
- iOS: Login with Cursor in the browser, return to the app
- Official: Cmd-D voice dictation; easier remote computer from your phone

CREATE A BOT
- New in the sidebar or Cmd/Ctrl+N, then Create new agent
- Short name, one primary job; standing rules in the description
- Start with about six roles; give each Bot recurring work
- Pin, hide, group into sections; account limit 50 Bots and group chats
- No model picker yet

HOW TO WRITE A TASK
- Outcome, sources, constraints, deliverable, review point
- Safe first task: attach a file and ask for a cited summary
- Then save a skill or routine
- Official examples: email cleanup, Starlink flights, build+buy+deploy a site, meetings, sales, refunds, podcast digest
- Testers: paste a viral video and recreate it; start from an org chart

AGENT COMPUTER AND LOGINS
- Open Agent Computer to watch; take over for password, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment
- Never paste passwords or one-time codes into chat
- Browser sessions persist and are shared across Bots
- Durable files in /workspace
- Settings → Beta: Update / Recover / Reset Agent Computer

PLUGINS AND CONNECTORS
- Settings → Plugins, then Add
- Type @ for a connector, / for a skill
- Multiple accounts can connect to the same plugin
- Testers: Grok Bot can connect to X and read X bookmarks

SKILLS AND ROUTINES
- Skill = reusable how-to; Routine = when to run it
- Teach a task: demo up to 10 minutes, review the draft skill
- A Bot can own 50 routines; deleting a routine has no undo

MULTI BOT TEAMS
- One Bot owns the outcome; add specialists when the role is stable
- Bots can message each other; they share the computer
- Keep send, buy, delete, publish behind approval

IOS
- Same Bots, chats, routines, plugins, and cloud computer
- Take over for login/2FA from the phone
- Pause or resume a routine on iOS; editing schedules still needs desktop

APPROVALS AND SAFETY
- Put the stop line in the request: draft, do not send
- Desktop: Allow once, Deny, or Always allow
- Start read-only; keep spend, send, publish, delete behind approval

FIRST BOTS WORTH CREATING
- Inbox, calendar, research/daily brief, coding, chief-of-staff, errands, content
- Chief-of-staff can turn the digest into a morning podcast

title: The TOP 10 Grok Bots you NEED to install now: #1 Bot Advisor Designs...
headline: The TOP 10 Grok Bots you NEED to install now: #1 Bot Advisor Designs and orders your entire Bot team without creating unnecessary agents.
body:
The TOP 10 Grok Bots you NEED to install now:

#1 Bot Advisor
Designs and orders your entire Bot team without creating unnecessary agents. Diagnoses noisy/overlapping Bots, decides if new work needs a new Bot, an existing one, a skill, or a one-off task. Always drafts a spec before creating anything.

#2 Chief of Staff
The single front door across priorities, Slack, Notion, Linear, and your specialists. Doesn't do the work, routes it. Keeps a compact register of owner/next step/blocker/due date. Every check-in surfaces decisions, not activity.

#3 Automation Scout
Finds repetitive work from evidence across Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear. Proposes exactly two candidates, runs the winner in shadow mode first (no real actions), only builds a recurring routine after a second successful test.

#4 Find the Signal
Detects patterns only visible across separate meetings and Slack threads, a concern raised in multiple rooms, a topic migrating to the center. Every signal ships with evidence, confidence level, and an alternative explanation. "No strong signal" is a valid result.

#5 Meeting Prep Brief
One short mobile brief before your first meeting, pulled from Calendar, Salesforce, Gmail, Slack, Granola, Gong. Who you're meeting, what changed, open loops, what to ask or decide. Unavailable sources are labeled NOT CHECKED, never guessed.

#6 X Account Crew
A 5-bot X workflow: Ideator finds angles, Hook Writer drafts in your voice, Planner manages the queue, Analyst tracks performance vs competitors, DM Manager surfaces real opportunities. Zero autonomous posting, nothing goes out without approval.

#7 Competitor Website Watch
Flags meaningful competitor changes, pricing, packaging, positioning, feature claims, while ignoring cookie-banner-level noise. Every finding includes before/after screenshots, exact URLs, timestamps. Failed captures are flagged, never mistaken for "no change."

#8 Engineering Agent Manager
Coordinates dev Bots across Linear and GitHub without overlapping work or unreviewed merges. Splits tickets into non-overlapping requirements, one owner each, flags dependency order. Nothing merges, deploys, or ships without your review of the diff and tests.

#9 Subscription Pruner
Finds subscriptions from email evidence, receipts, renewals, trial notices. Builds a keep/review/cancel list, acts only on approved items. Never touches passwords, 2FA, or payment confirmation, those stay with you. Full before/after action log.

#10 Grocery Autopilot
Plans the week, builds Amazon/Costco carts, coordinates meals with your calendar. Learns household rules once (allergies, budget, brands), shows the full cart and price comparison before checkout. Never buys without explicit approval.

body:
I tested every AI assistant setup and they all reset the second you close the window.

Grok Bot does not.

You show it a workflow once, it saves it and runs it forever.

No re-explaining, no prompt library to maintain, and no restarting every session as if you're beginning from scratch.

Every other assistant treats each conversation like the first one. You built something last week and this week you are copy-pasting prompts like it never happened.

Grok Bot remembers everything. Files. Browser sessions. Preferences. The way you work. It keeps compounding context instead of dumping it.

Multiple Bots share one computer. They run in parallel, message each other and then pass tasks without you routing every single thing between them.

This is not a better ChatGPT.

It is a completely different build.

I wrote the full setup guide because most people have no idea this exists and they are still stuck re-teaching their assistant basic stuff every morning.

title: grok bot + a second auditor bot is basically a tiny research team...
headline: grok bot + a second auditor bot is basically a tiny research team running itself i gave one agent the market research job.
body:
grok bot + a second auditor bot is basically a tiny research team running itself

i gave one agent the market research job. it pulled 20+ sources, noticed the numbers were measuring different things, then handed the comparison to another bot before writing the brief.

here’s how i set it up (in 5 mins)

1. create a Research Chief and give it the full research workflow
2. create a Source Auditor whose only job is checking claims, scopes and conflicting numbers
3. save the rules + previous corrections so the next run doesn’t start from zero
4. give the Chief a new topic and let it delegate verification to the Auditor automatically

the wild part is i never told it mid-run to call the second bot. it hit the verification step and delegated the work itself.

kimi memory loop makes this even more interesting: skills keep the workflow, constraints keep the corrections, and the context graph keeps what both agents discovered.

title: I came across an interesting issue with Grok @bot Sometimes it assumes...
headline: I came across an interesting issue with Grok @bot Sometimes it assumes something is true without full validation or context, and writes it straight into the bot's identity Here's how I handle it 👇 I paste a write rule...
body:
I came across an interesting issue with Grok @bot 

Sometimes it assumes something is true without full validation or context, and writes it straight into the bot's identity

Here's how I handle it 👇

I paste a write rule into every new bot that splits memory into 3 drawers:

1. Profile: The stable identity, loaded into the prompt every turn. The one place a stray "maybe" or an old product line should never sneak into.
2. Log: Dated history, one line per event. What happened, not who the bot is.
3. Note: This week's blocker or pending item. Drops off the always-visible list once it's ranked low, but stays on disk until you Forget it.

Here's the exact block:

"PROFILE MEMORY
Write to own profile only when the fact is stable and needed every turn.
Test: if forgotten tomorrow, this agent does the job wrong every day. Else do not write profile.
Profile scope: [lane coordinates] + [rules they mark stable]. Nothing else.
If unsure, do not write profile. If it reads like a diary, it is log.

LOG MEMORY
Write when it reconstructs what happened and is not needed every turn.
Log scope: [dated lane events]. One line. No chat diary. No profile repeats.

NOTE MEMORY
Write only when it should drop off the always-visible list once it's ranked low.
The platform fades it from the prompt. It stays on disk until Forget.
Test: useless next week is note. Needed every turn is profile. Worth finding next month is log.
Note scope: [this-week blocker / pending]."

Set this once and one stray chat never rewrites who the bot is.

title: everyone is looking at grok bot like it is five new employees the more...
headline: everyone is looking at grok bot like it is five new employees the more interesting part is that they are not five isolated employees they share one persistent cloud environment: the same browser sessions, terminal,...
body:
everyone is looking at grok bot like it is five new employees

the more interesting part is that they are not five isolated employees

they share one persistent cloud environment: the same browser sessions, terminal, filesystem and authenticated tools - while a chief of staff can route work between them without waiting for you to open the laptop

that turns one login into infrastructure

a research bot can collect leads, pass them to a writer, hand the result to a designer and let an ops bot update the workflow all inside the same running machine

the upside is obvious: less copying, fewer handoffs and work that continues while you sleep

the blast radius is just as obvious:

- authenticate only the services the whole agent fleet is allowed to reach
- give every bot a narrow role description, because that description becomes its place in the org chart
- keep irreversible actions behind human approval: sending, publishing, spending and production changes
- store skills, configuration and long-term state inside `/workspace`, because the rest of the VM may disappear during an update
- treat shared sessions as shared authority, not as separate bot identities

the same architecture that makes grok bot useful is what makes it dangerous to configure casually

my take: the breakthrough is not that you can hire five AI workers

it is that they can operate like one persistent company inside your real tools and your job changes from prompting every task to designing the permissions, boundaries and handoffs

the full chief-of-staff setup, session handoff model, approval matrix and `/workspace` survival strategy are mapped out in the article ↓

title: Here's how you can use Grok Bot to make $$$ I actually figure out how...
headline: Here's how you can use Grok Bot to make $$$ I actually figure out how to use Grok Bot to manage my software.
body:
Here's how you can use Grok Bot to make $$$

I actually figure out how to use Grok Bot to manage my software.

So I run 100% of my payment, affiliate, customer service and paid ads infrastructure on Whop.

Whop is actually better than stripe for payments because I know I can get ahold of someone there if something goes wrong.

Stripe would just ban you and tell you to kick rocks.

I also save like $500+/mo in software just by being on top of their infrastructure.

I don't pay for affiliate management, paid ads attribution or customer service software, it's all included.

They announced an official connector with Grok Bot and let me tell you, this is GOOD.

Just by connecting it to my whop, it was able to pull an analysis of my businesses and how they are doing.

It told me about the growth, pit falls and what to watch out in the future.

It did this in seconds of connecting it with nothing else.

But I managed to make it better.

Now, before I go into the weeds of everything. I want to give you a heads up.

It does give Grok Bot full admin control, so make sure you disable all "delete" access from Grok Bot.

At the end of the day, I don't want Grok Bot to delete something like a product plan or a cancel a user by accident.

I want to handle that myself.

So the more I got more into it, I realized that you can have ONE general Grok Bot that handles everything and it does pretty well.

But I highly recommend you have several bots with different profiles.

Profiles allow you to give a "purpose" to each bot.

And I figured out that if you give it a JSON context profile in the description, it works better than just writing a paragraph.

Why a JSON? Because I want it to know what kind of access it should prioritized.

You can't give each bot custom configs for the connectors, but if it has a JSON it's pretty good at respecting what it's supposed to do.

So if you want a Bot to only focus on X business on Whop, you make a bot with the access it should be allowed to do and what business it's managing.

I have a Customer Service Bot, a Growth Bot, a Whop Ads Bot.

Customer Service reports daily if there's any pending issues, resolutions that need to be handled, etc.

The Growth Bot is in charge of tracking KPIs for my business growth.

And the Whop Ads one is trained on my media buying preferences.

You can setup routines that make the bot wake up and perform an operation.

Because Whop CLI works natively with all of whop's features, I don't need to use the linux computer that it spins up for you.

But if I needed it to go and browse the web or perform a task that only a VA can manually do, it can do that too!

Honestly this is great and I can't wait to use it more, will keep you guys updated.

headline: whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense someone on SpaceXAI's own sales team says he showed Grok Bot one job, stopped checking its work, and now calls himself 2 to 3 times more efficient: the manual for the...
body:
whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense

someone on SpaceXAI's own sales team says he showed Grok Bot one job, stopped checking its work, and now calls himself 2 to 3 times more efficient: the manual for the same product says a test run performs real work, so it navigates websites, changes files and calls every tool you connected

turns out the whole change is a time of day. you give the job once with a time attached, and the same job comes back finished every morning without you starting it

i ran three of mine on a daily time for a week and read back what they had actually done: two had fired every morning i asked for, and the third had switched itself off on day 4 because i never answered it

Grok Bot calls a job on a clock a routine, and one bot will carry 50 of them while keeping only the last 20 runs of each:

set your first one tonight in one chat window, 3 moves:

1. say the job, the time it goes off and the one action it must ask you about first, all in a single message

2. have it run that job once right now on something safe to get wrong, because the practice run really sends, really files and really clicks

3. tell it what to do on a morning when the thing it reads is missing, so you get a message about it instead of yesterday's answer copied forward

50 jobs on a clock against 20 remembered runs is the real trade: run 21 replaces run 1, and it would rather pause a job and ask you than carry one into a month nobody was reading

title: One change took my Grok Bot agent's output from 50% done to 90% done
headline: One change took my Grok Bot agent's output from 50% done to 90% done.
body:
One change took my Grok Bot agent's output from 50% done to 90% done.

The bot runs a QA loop on its own work first.

Here's how it works:
- Agent finishes a first pass
- It builds a panel of sub-agents from the rest of the team
- The panel runs an adversarial review
- Three rounds of that, then it comes to me

You can't start here, though. 

You have to be in the weeds with your agent team, giving the feedback yourself until it knows what good looks like, before any of it runs on its own.

Then take the thread where you gave all that feedback and use it as the basis for a feedback skill.

The next agent to review will review exactly like you.

title: Grok bot might be the first tool that lets a non-technical person run...
headline: Grok bot might be the first tool that lets a non-technical person run an entire business with a team of ai agents, no engineering background required.
body:
Grok bot might be the first tool that lets a non-technical person run an entire business with a team of ai agents, no engineering background required.

here's how to actually set it up well.

1. one mission per setup. agents run on a shared cloud computer, so mixing your newsletter, your social posting, and your admin work into one setup creates context bloat and burns through tokens fast. scope each bot to one job.

2. start with a chief of staff. give it access to your existing docs, notion, slack, gmail, whatever you actually use, have it audit the business, then tell you the top three agents worth building first to actually move revenue.

3. prove a task works before you hire for it. have the chief of staff do the task once manually, review the output yourself, and only then say "now build a bot that does exactly that." earn each new agent by proving the task first, don't hire speculatively.

4. the constraints are the feature, not the limitation. a limited number of agent slots, one thread per bot, like dming a teammate, forces you to stay mission-oriented instead of spinning up a bot for every passing idea.

5. you make the calls, not the agent. endless tinkering over where content should live or how a process should work is a trap. at some point you decide, commit, and move on. the agent executes your decision, it doesn't make it for you.

6. run week one with zero new agents. just learn the actual system, execute with what you already have. week three or so is when the real gaps become obvious and expansion actually makes sense, not before.

7. add recurring routines last. once the core setup is proven, ask your chief of staff what recurring jobs would genuinely move the business forward overnight, and let it build the automations that run while you sleep.

body:
📝Grok Botをトライアルで使ってみた→速攻でトークン燃え尽きた、、、けど、所感をシェア

AIエージェントを”使っている”という感覚無しで使えるイメージ

簡単レベルは
Grok Bot＞Codex＞Claude Codeデスクトップ

AIエージェントを”使う”という点ではトップクラスでわかりやすい気がする、というか逆に何も設定無しでチャッピーに話しかけるような感覚でどんどんAIエージェント（Grok Bot）が動く

例えば、Gmailやスプレッドシートに繋ぎたいと思ったら、チャット欄の流れに追加するプラグインやコネクタが出てきて、そのまま追加して会話が継続される

このUXはかなり良い。普通ならメニューのコネクタやプラグインから入れたいものを探して事前に入れておくけど、Grok Botは動きながら必要ならどんどん流れで入れていく、これはユーザーにとってストレスフリー

それからiOSアプリのGrok Botもあるけど、これCodexのリモートと同じレベルで操作できる
つまり、デスクトップPC、ノートPCで作業しているGrok Botの会話をそのままスマホから確認できて指示もできる。これが最初からできるのは素晴らしい

一方で、クラウド上のエージェントだから、制御するためのCLAUDE.mdやAGENTS.mdなどが無くてわかりにくい。というか、「こういうルールにしてくれ」と依頼するとクラウド側の共有メモリーに保存してくれる。このへんの仕組みを調べるためのトークンは足りなかった

また、色々調べると、作ったbotが消えてしまった事件なども発生しているので、その対策指示文をnemopiさんが公開されていたので入れておいた。こういった事前対策は本当に大事

あと、Grok Botが使える料金プランがメチャクチャわかりにくい。SuperGrok Plus $100？Cursor Pro+ $60？など、人によっては$100に誘導されてそっちを契約しちゃいそう

とりあえず、Grok Botをもっと使うなら、トライアルは全然足りないので、最低でも$60（約1万円弱）が必要ですね、もう少し遊びまっす！

body:
以下是完整繁體中文翻譯：

每一個你過去使用過的 AI 工具，都在等你。
你打開瀏覽器分頁、輸入提示、等待回應、複製輸出、再貼到真正的工作裡。一旦你闔上筆電，執行就立刻停止。
Grok Bot 徹底顛覆了這個模式。
它不再運行在短暫的聊天視窗裡，而是讓每一個 Grok Bot 代理人擁有專屬的雲端虛擬機器——配備持久化的網頁瀏覽器、終端機、檔案系統，以及背景行程執行器。
當你晚上 11 點闔上筆電時，你的 Bot 仍持續運作：掃描競爭對手、執行瀏覽器自動化、協調外展草稿、在資料中心執行排程任務。
這是一份完整的 Grok Bot 架構指南：如何設計多代理人團隊、安全的工作階段交接、用螢幕示範自動化複雜視覺工作流程、強制嚴格的可逆性防護機制，以及掌握隱藏的 /workspace 持久化技巧，保護你的代理人基礎設施免受雲端 VM 更新影響。
不需要任何基礎設施經驗。
典範轉移：從「提示」到「委派」
要真正發揮 Grok Bot 的價值，你必須停止把 AI 當作對話式助理，開始把它當作一支自主的數位勞動力。
當你把工作委派給 Grok Bot 代理人時，你不是寫一個提示，而是給它一份角色章程（role charter）：明確的職權範圍、可連接的工具組，以及自主執行必須停止、需要人類核准的清晰界線。
第一步：設計「幕僚長」拓撲結構
新手最常犯的錯誤，是一次創建十幾個互不協調的 Bot，然後自己手動管理。這只會造成聊天混亂，也徹底違背自動化的初衷。
正確做法是部署幕僚長拓撲（Chief of Staff Topology）：
五個核心專家角色
1幕僚長（Klaus）：人類操作者的唯一入口。它接收高層目標、拆解成子任務、委派給專家、並彙整最終報告。
2首席偵察員（Mara）：研究潛在客戶、掃描競爭對手網站、監控市場趨勢，並把結構化潛在客戶檔案輸出到 /workspace/state/。
3文案撰寫員（Cole）：讀取 Mara 的原始研究資料，撰寫符合你品牌語氣的個人化外展信件、部落格文章或電子報大綱。
4視覺設計師（Rina）：根據文案指示，使用無頭瀏覽器引擎或設計工具產出橫幅圖與 UI 截圖。
5營運追蹤員（Vince）：監控回覆、更新專案看板（ClickUp / Notion），並在需要人類介入時發出警示。
組織圖規則
在 Grok Bot 中，Bot 的個人檔案描述就是它在團隊組織圖上的職位說明。
當 Klaus 收到請求時，它會掃描工作區內所有可用 Bot 的描述。如果 Mara 的描述明確寫著「負責市場研究、潛在客戶發掘與競爭對手爬取」，Klaus 就會自動把研究任務轉給 Mara，無需人類介入。
第二步：安全的工作階段交接（不用貼密碼）
傳統 AI 工具要求你把機密 API 金鑰或帳號密碼直接貼到聊天訊息裡——這會把憑證暴露在日誌檔與上下文視窗中。
Grok Bot 使用互動式工作階段交接：
1Bot 用它的雲端瀏覽器導航到受保護的工具（例如 LinkedIn、Notion、Gmail 或內部 CRM）。
2當它遇到登入牆或 2FA 提示時，Bot 會暫停，並向你的桌面應用程式發送「Agent Computer」畫面請求。
3你開啟即時雲端瀏覽器畫面，親自輸入憑證或完成 2FA 驗證，然後點擊「完成」。
4Bot 取得已驗證的工作階段權杖，而你的底層密碼永遠不會暴露給 AI 模型或聊天紀錄。
因為你帳號下的所有 Bot 共享同一個底層雲端環境，一次驗證某個服務後，整個代理人團隊都能使用該活躍工作階段。
整合管道（原生 vs. Composio）
•原生外掛：使用內建一鍵連接器連接核心工具（Google Drive、Notion、Slack、AWS）。
•Composio / 外部橋接：對於沒有原生整合的平台（YouTube API、Reddit、LinkedIn、GoHighLevel、Perplexity），把 Composio 當作主外掛連接。在共享知識庫中存放規則，讓所有 Bot 知道可透過 Composio 存取擴充工具。
第三步：用「教任務」（Teach-a-Task）自動化視覺工作流程
用文字解釋多步驟 UI 工作流程既繁瑣又容易誤解。如果任務涉及點擊特定儀表板篩選器、下載 CSV、再把數字複製到試算表，不如直接視覺示範。
如何使用「教任務」：
1在 Grok Bot 桌面客戶端開啟 Bot 的 Agent Computer 畫面。
2點擊「Teach a Task」開始螢幕錄製。
3在雲端瀏覽器上手動執行完整工作流程：開啟儀表板、套用篩選器、匯出資料、貼到目標文件。
4點擊「停止錄製」。
Grok Bot 會分析 DOM 事件與視覺滑鼠動作，合成步驟，並產生可重複使用的 Skill 檔案。
精煉產生的 Skill
錄製完成後，加入明確的錯誤處理指令來精煉產生的 Skill。
第四步：強制執行可逆性核准矩陣
一支 24/7 運作的自主代理人，如果被允許執行不可逆的真實世界動作而沒有監督，很快就會造成混亂。
為了防止未經授權的動作，必須執行可逆性原則（Reversibility Principle）：
把核准界線寫進 Bot 章程
每一個 Bot 的個人檔案描述結尾都必須加上明確的界線條款：
角色：外展文案撰寫員（Cole） 範圍：從 /workspace/state/leads.json 讀取潛在客戶資料並撰寫個人化電子郵件草稿。 界線規則：你有完整權限進行研究、摘要並將電子郵件草稿儲存到資料庫。你絕對不能點擊「傳送」或在沒有人類明確審核與聊天

body:
whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense

Danny Limanseta was making his game's artwork by hand, one picture at a time, until he handed the job to Grok Bot and got 74 finished pieces back in about 2 hours: the cheapest way in for one person was $200 a month at launch and it is $60 today

he is a product designer by day, so he pushed it at his real job next: he handed over a written spec and got the screens laid out and the wireframes built from scratch

turns out the way in is a recording. you open the bot's screen, press record, and do the job once while it watches, up to ten minutes, and it writes its own instructions off what it saw

that recording becomes a skill it keeps. a skill with a time on it becomes a routine, and the routine runs on a computer in the cloud, so it keeps going after you shut the laptop

i tried it last night on the thing i am worst at and barely typed: i pointed at what was wrong and said no, over and over, and the version that survived is the one in the video

five moves that get a person with no drawing hand a usable result tonight:

- show it one finished thing you already like before you ask for anything, because it copies a standard far better than it copies a description
- record the boring middle of the job, the part you would never think to write down, and close every private tab before you start
- have it make five and correct all five, since your corrections are the part it actually keeps
- only then say save that as a skill, and only then put it on a clock
- start on work you would not mind getting wrong in public

SpaceXAI puts the ceiling in its own manual: what comes out of that recording is a draft, and the decision rules, the failure handling and the "stop and ask me" line are still yours to add

it is 70% off what it cost at launch and there is a free trial running, which is why your feed filled up this week with people shipping things they cannot personally make

bookmark this. the video is my own evening on it: 24,000 threads wrapped around a black hole, turning on measurements a telescope actually took, and i have never modelled anything in 3D in my life

body:
「Grok BotがAIエージェントの市場を食い尽くそうとしている」

対話型のチャット画面でプロンプトを工夫する活用から、常時稼働する実行環境を持つエージェントへの移行が進んでいる。

xAIのGrok Botは専用のクラウド実行環境とブラウザ視覚操作、リアルタイムなXデータ連携を兼ね備えた実行レイヤーとして設計されている。

特徴は以下の4点。

① 常時稼働する専用クラウド環境
各Botにブラウザ、ファイルシステム、ログインセッションを保持したクラウドPCが個別に割り当てられている。

利用者が端末を閉じても、バックグラウンドで調査タスクやスクリプト実行を完結できます。

② リアルタイムなXデータとWebテレメトリの直接連携
学習データのカットオフ期間に縛られず、X上のリアルタイムな会話データや市場の声を直近数時間単位で取得できる。

ニュースや検索エンジンに掲載される前の初期シグナルを検知する用途に適しています。

③ API未提供サービスを動かすNo-APIアプローチ
Webツールの8割以上はエージェント向けAPIを持たない。

Grok Botは人間と同様に画面の視覚認識とブラウザ制御を用いて、CRMや社内ポータルを直接操作する。

④ 並列マルチエージェントによる多角検証
単一の指示文による線形処理にとどまらず、脆弱性監査、速度検証、構造再設計など役割を分担したサブエージェントを並列起動して結果を統合する。

以下実際に使えそうな例。

・市場と競合の監査
Xやフォーラムにおける直近30日の生の声からボトルネックを抽出し、自社製品の改善や差別化方針の策定に繋げる。

・リード調査と提案文作成
最新のWeb情報や投稿内容から商談相手の直近課題を把握し、個別提案文の下書きを作成する。

・コードやワークフローの自律検証
クラウド環境内でコードのリファクタリングからテスト実行、修正提案までを一連のジョブとして回す。

title: This is how I setup my Grok Bot and its been super fun to use: - I...
headline: This is how I setup my Grok Bot and its been super fun to use: - I setup 1 bot as my clone (Brantley Bot) and had my Chat GPT, my Manus, and my Gemini give me summaries of who I am, my goals, my work, etc.
body:
This is how I setup my Grok Bot and its been super fun to use:

- I setup 1 bot as my clone (Brantley Bot) and had my Chat GPT, my Manus, and my Gemini give me summaries of who I am, my goals, my work, etc. I then gave those summaries to Brantley Bot.

- Now Brantley Bot creates, and talks, to any bot I need for certain jobs.

For example I told Brantley Bot I needed to have an expert do my Fantasy Football draft for me; now I have a Draft Bot who will be ready for my leagues draft time tonight.

Don't worry my family knows I am using AI for fantasy football and I actually got last place last year but I have high hopes for this year.

Brantley Bot then checks in with the other bots and will update me or give them prompts so I only ever talk to Brantley Bot, just the way I set it up.

Of course I can talk to the other bots but I don't want to if I don't have to.

Anything I need Brantley Bot can either do it or spinup another bot to do it.

headline: Grok Bot by Elon Musk just replaced a $398,000 boutique law firm's contract desk.
body:
Grok Bot by Elon Musk just replaced a $398,000 boutique law firm's contract desk. Six AI agents, $220 a month, doing the redlines associates bill $650 an hour for

Every prompt he used is public - this isn't a theory, it's a build anyone can copy.

Here's the old retainer, broken down:

> $18,000 a year for the Westlaw subscription
> $40,000 for a contract-review SaaS seat
> $85,000 for outside counsel retainer on overflow review
> $65,000 for the paralegal who preps every file
> $190,000 for the junior associate who redlines until 1am so a partner can sign off before the deadline

$398,000 a year. The agents cost $2,640. Same coverage, 150 times cheaper, and it never misses a filing deadline.

The workload got split six ways - every agent runs on its own cloud machine, and everything lands in one shared case file.

> INTAKE reads every incoming contract against the firm's playbook and flags any clause outside standard terms
> REDLINE drafts the first-pass markup overnight so the associate starts from a document, not a blank page
> PRECEDENT searches the firm's own closed deals for the last time this exact clause got negotiated and how it ended
> CONFLICTS checks every new counterparty and their affiliates against the active client list before anyone signs an engagement letter
> DEADLINE tracks every closing condition and notice period across every open matter and pings 48 hours before anything lapses
> CHIEF OF STAFF reads the other five at 7am, ranks what actually needs a partner's eyes, and sends the priority list before the first coffee

A single associate can realistically run maybe 15 matters at once. The six agents run 150 without dropping a deadline.

Teach the playbook once, and it holds for every contract after that - no laptop required to keep it running.

The whole review-desk model assumed nobody could read fast enough and every hour of a lawyer's time was expensive. Neither of those is true anymore.

So the partner opens their inbox, reads the priority list for five minutes, and knows exactly which contracts need a human read today. That used to be a first-year associate's entire year, and they billed 2,400 hours doing it.

title: whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense someone at SpaceXAI...
headline: whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense someone at SpaceXAI wrote the ceiling into the Grok Bot documentation and left the page up: one bot will hold 50 standing jobs and put every one of them on a clock, but...
body:
whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense

someone at SpaceXAI wrote the ceiling into the Grok Bot documentation and left the page up: one bot will hold 50 standing jobs and put every one of them on a clock, but it keeps only the last 20 runs of each, so run 21 deletes run 1 and the office quietly forgets the morning it did the work

i ran three of mine on a daily time for two weeks and then went looking for what they had actually done: the two quiet ones still had their whole history, the busy one had already dropped its first nine mornings, and a folder i kept myself was the only place that work still existed

Grok Bot is worth building an office around, and you can make it keep receipts before the second job exists:

- tell every job to write its result somewhere you own, a doc or a sheet or a message to yourself, because the app holds 20 runs and then starts writing over them
- run each job by hand once before you give it a time, on something safe to get wrong, since the practice run is the live run and it really sends and really files
- keep one job per bot instead of stacking them, as a bot works one screen at a time and four jobs on one bot stand in line behind each other
- answer it when it checks in, because after a long enough silence it asks whether you still want the schedule and switches the job off when nothing comes back
- put the one action it must ask you about into the job itself, as an approval stops the next step and leaves whatever already ran exactly where it landed
- look at the history every week rather than every month, since a daily job burns through all 20 of its remembered runs in under three weeks

turns out the office is the easy half and the paper trail is the hard one: 50 jobs on a clock against 20 remembered runs each means the busier a job gets, the less of it you can still see, so the first work you hand over should be the work you would have to prove you did

my take, and it is the arguable one: you keep the record, everything else is rented, and everybody builds the office in one evening and the filing cabinet never

title: How to use Grok Bot to run your business: Pick one business
headline: How to use Grok Bot to run your business: Pick one business.
body:
How to use Grok Bot to run your business:

Pick one business.

It can be a newsletter, a Shopify store, a directory, or another single project.

Do not mix that business with your inbox, receipts, social accounts, and several side projects. Grok Bot will mix files and instructions between them while burning the tokens needed for the real work.

Then build the team in this order.

Start with one chief of staff.

Connect the documents and tools used by the business.

Then ask:

“Take stock of this business. Which three agents should we create first to drive revenue?”

The chief of staff must understand the business before it can manage the work.

Let it do each job once.

Do not create specialist agents from guesses.

Have the chief of staff perform the task. Review the result. Fix the process.

When the job works, turn that proven process into a specialist agent.

Run the first team for a week.

Do not add more agents. Do not keep changing the skills.

Use the team and watch where the work gets stuck.

Add agents only for real gaps.

If the chief of staff keeps repeating the same task, give that task to a specialist.

If an agent has no mission-critical job, remove it.

Give every agent a short report.

Keep each update to five lines covering three things:

What shipped.
What is stuck.
What needs you.
The chief of staff can use those reports to route work and bring a human into the jobs that are blocked.
Turn proven work into routines.

Ask:

“Based on how we worked this week, which jobs should become routines or skills?”

Schedule the research, inbox checks, reports, follow-ups, and other work that repeats.

Move fixed work out of Grok Bot.

If a job is predictable and high-volume, run it with a script or a cheaper automation.

Keep Grok Bot on work that needs judgment: choosing, filtering, coordinating, reviewing, and recommending.

Keep the human in charge.

Agents can execute the work. The human still chooses the process and approves decisions where the wording, strategy, or risk matters.

Build the team.

Run it.

Find the gaps.

Then automate.

That is how you use Grok Bot to run a business instead of building another AI setup you never use.
